subject: literature
passage: For three weeks, old Mr. Castellano had said nothing about Divya's bread except "Again." She had kneaded, shaped, and baked loaf after loaf, and each time he had broken one open, studied the inside, and pushed the tray back toward her. On Friday, he broke open her loaf and looked at it for a long while. Then, without a word, he set the rest of her loaves in the front window beside his own, where every customer would see them. Mr. Castellano's action most likely indicates that he ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: now considered Divya's bread good enough to offer to his customers.
choices.B: wanted his customers to see how much Divya's bread still needed work.
choices.C: had decided to stop teaching Divya because she was not improving.
choices.D: regretted having been so harsh with Divya during her first weeks.

explanation.why: For weeks Mr. Castellano rejected every loaf. On Friday, instead of saying "Again," he placed her loaves in the front window beside his own, where customers would see them. Displaying the bread with his own shows he finally judged it good enough to sell.
explanation.A: Correct. Putting her loaves in the shop window next to his own, after weeks of rejecting them, signals approval.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A baker would not display bread beside his own to show customers its flaws; the change from "Again" signals approval, not criticism.
explanation.C: Incorrect. He did not push the tray back this time, and he displayed her bread, which suggests she had improved.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text shows him approving her bread but gives no sign that he regrets how he treated her.
